Two of Telltale's earlier matters are Hartwell and Delmore. Hartwell supplies all the examples below. I've left Delmore out because the client's instruction is that no strategy or work product from that matter be shared with other Telltale counsel unless General Counsel Marguerite Salvesen asks. Its protective order also limits produced material to that action. If you need Delmore, get Ms. Salvesen's clearance first.

**Hartwell v. Telltale Cardiac Systems (Ashgrove County, No. 25-CV-03817), AL-4120 pacing lead**

1. **The 2020 field engineer note.** It observed that returned leads showed wear from repeated bending near the pocket and suggested the design be revisited. As of the October 7, 2025 memo it had not been produced, and the associate called it the most damaging undisclosed document. It bears directly on notice and design, and it is the kind of item that surfaces in a responsive search. Look for informal field-engineer observations on returned product, not just formal reports.

2. **The "Larkspur review" (2021) and the 2021 trend report.** Larkspur was an internal quality inquiry into returned-lead fractures. It preceded the 2021 trend report, which plaintiff will use to argue Telltale had notice of a rising fracture rate. As of the October 2025 memo, plaintiff had not asked about Larkspur by name. Plaintiff's June 2025 requests for complaint and returned-product analyses and fatigue testing could still reach it. Look for code-named quality inquiries and trend reports, and ask the client early what exists and what is privileged.

3. **Orrinwick, the complaint database.** Orrinwick is the system behind the figure of 31 confirmed conductor fractures in about 22,000 leads shipped (about 0.14%). Engineering still has to confirm that rate stayed within the labeled range. The scope fights centered on it. The parties agreed on June 18, 2025 that AL-4120 records would run from the 2018 clinical-use start to the November 15, 2022 revision. Telltale refused post-revision events from the implanting center. Plaintiff also pushed for ArcLine-family-wide records, and Telltale offered only an informal AL-4120/AL-4125 coil-difference declaration, expressly not a concession of family-wide relevance. Expect to be asked what Orrinwick contains, how it is searched, and how far back and across which models.

Hartwell involves no cross-matter restriction that I can see in the file. The client did ask that design and complaint-handling records be treated as confidential, with a protective order proposed before any production.
